sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale International Distribution of Acetate Eyeglass Frames

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law with Common Law influences in commercial matters)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA) in force since 2012

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (as amended by Law 70 of 2019 and Decree 129 of 2020) adopting the FATF Recommendations; Executive Decree 363 of 2015 on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing; provisions of the Private Interest Foundations Law (Law 25 of 12 June 1995) requiring identification of founders, council members, and beneficiaries; and the Unified UBO Registry established under the Fintech Law (Law 159 of 2020) requiring central registry disclosure of ultimate beneficial owners of all juridical entities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency (PIF Council Members and Founder Custodian)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) via the foundation's designated resident agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama is party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of the Private Interest Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Paz y Salvo) for the Foundation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Registry of Panama and Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Legalized Power of Attorney granted to the Resident Agent (Abogado/Agencia)
Certified Translation of the Foundation Bylaws (Reglamento) into English or Spanish
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified Public Translator (Traducción Pública) in Panama or country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence (EDD) for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined under Title II of Law 23 of 2015; obligatory screening of all founded and council members, beneficiaries, and beneficial owners against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Panamanian Ministry of Economy and Finance targeted financial sanctions list (Lista de Sancionados); risk-based approach requiring PEP flagging in the foundation's internal compliance policy and immediate reporting to the Financial Analysis Unit (Unidad de Análisis Financiero - UAF) on any match.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Panamá Emprende y Línea de Empresas y Personas (Módulo del Registro Público de Panamá) accessible via the Public Registry of Panama online portal and via the Plataforma: Registro Público en Línea (RPAL)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All registered names must be in Spanish or accepted Spanish transliteration of foreign names; the name may include English alphabet characters but must comply with Spanish orthographic rules; the name must end with a distinctive denomination indicating the foundation structure, such as 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or 'P.I.F.'; names must not be confusingly similar to existing registered entities; generic and geographic names require supporting documentation and prior approval; accented Latin characters and special typography are generally restricted to standard Spanish letterforms.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant's resident agent must file a formal written appeal (Recurso de Apelación) with the Dirección General del Registro Público de Panamá within 10 business days of the rejection notice; the appeal must clearly demonstrate that the proposed name does not conflict with existing registrations and complies with all statutory naming restrictions; the Registro Público shall issue a final administrative decision within 30 business days; if the appeal is denied, the applicant may initiate a fresh reservation for an alternative name and retain the right to file a separate judicial challenge (Demanda Contencioso-Administrativa) before the Third Administrative Chamber of the Supreme Court of Justice (Sala Tercera de la Corte Suprema de Justicia) within 60 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Whether virtual offices are accepted for the target industry depends on the foundation's actual registered office in Panama and the resident agent's physical presence in Panama. A domestic registered office is statutorily required, but business operations including wholesale distribution are substantially permitted from foreign jurisdictions; the commercial bank and tax authorities require a Panama resident agent with a permanent physical address. Where the foundation conducts no physical local activities, a virtual office is generally acceptable subject to the resident agent providing a verifiable fixed address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate (estimated 15 to 30% probability within 24 months). The DGI and the Municipality of Panama carry out unannounced on-site inspections to verify the existence and active operation of the foundation's domicile and to enforce compliance with territorial tax obligations; lower risk if the foundation has no local revenue, holds no local real estate, and is not a resident taxpayer, but do not consider the inspection risk to be negligible and always keep the resident agent's address and records updated.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal consultation and compliance advice for the foundation's non-resident wholesale distribution structure

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark hourly rate for cross-border corporate due diligence and AML compliance advice

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley N° 25 de 12 de junio de 1995, as amended (Private Interest Foundations Law), particularly Articles 5, 6, 12, 15, 18, 19 and 24; complementary dispositions of the Código Civil and Código de Comercio as incorporated by Article 9 of Law 25.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado / Personas Jurídicas
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (notarial deed) filed for inscription in the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; the foundation must have an initial patrimony (endowment) adequate to fulfill its objectives. Customarily a nominal endowment of at least USD 10,000 is set out in the charter. No government escrow account is required; assets may be contributed at any time and remain accessible for lawful purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME], adopted this [DATE] in Panama City. The founder and subscribing parties unanimously resolve: (1) to approve and confirm the foundation charter as inscribed; (2) to subscribe an initial endowment of USD 10,000, evidenced by bank transfer; (3) to adopt the registered office at [address], Republic of Panama; (4) to appoint [NAME] as members of the Foundation Council, with powers specified in the charter; (5) to appoint [NAME] as Protector; and (6) to authorize the Council President and Secretary, jointly and severally, to open bank accounts, execute documents, and carry out all acts necessary for the lawful administration and international wholesale distribution of ophthalmic eyeglass frames. This resolution is immediately effective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engage Licensed Attorney and Prepare Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private notary public in Panama City (authorized by the Supreme Court of Justice)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retain a Panama-licensed attorney and notary. Draft the private foundation charter (Escritura Constitutiva) specifying foundation name, duration, patrimony, founder, beneficiaries, Foundation Council members, Protector, and registered office. Execute the draft before a Panamanian notary public.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the founder's passport or ID
Proof of lawful source of funds (bank reference letter)
Draft foundation charter with council and protector appointments
Notarial power of attorney if attorney acts on behalf of founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the charter, correct any factual inconsistencies, resubmit a firmado (countersigned) revised draft, and re-notarize; pay any additional notarial fee promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público (Escribano Público) designated by the Notarial Order of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the final charter with all required dossiers to the notary. The notary reads, authenticates, and records the deed as an Escritura Pública. Obtain notarial certified copies (testimonios) sufficient for registry filing and banking purposes.
required_dossiers: Foundation charter in executable form
Identification and signatures of all appearing parties
Notarial fee receipt
List of beneficiaries if required by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies gaps, remedy by executing an addendum to the charter and re-notarizing; expedite through the notary's office to avoid additional delays.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Oficina de Personas Jurídicas / Fundaciones
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the original notarized Escritura Pública plus certified copy to the Public Registry's Foundation Section. Pay the registry inscription fee. Await issuance of the certified copy of the registered Ficha (foundation record) and registration certificate (Certificado de Registro).
required_dossiers: Original notarized Escritura Pública de Constitución
Certified copy from the notary (testimonio)
Registry fee payment receipt (tasa única / arancel)
RUC (tax identification) registration application if applying simultaneously
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a defect (defecto) notice, cure the specific defect within 5 business days by filing corrective documents or a clarification addendum; if rejected, refile with corrected deed and new fee if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Tax Identification Number and Municipality Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipalidad del Distrito de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the foundation with DGI for tax identification (RUC) and, if the foundation engages in economic activity, obtain municipal Aviso de Operación from the local municipality. For pure holding/custodial foundations, Aviso de Operación may be unnecessary; however, the wholesale trading activity requires it.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of registered foundation Ficha
Notarized foundation charter
Identity of president/secretary or foundation council members
Municipal business license application form (Aviso de Operación)
Lease contract or title proving registered office location
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality requires an environmental or zoning query, provide the office lease contract and a floor plan; appeal any adverse zoning determination administratively within 30 days and concurrently apply for provisional operation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Bank Account and Activate Foundation Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) supervised licensed banks; Public Registry for governance filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first Foundation Council meeting, formally adopt the pro forma resolution, and open a corporate bank account in the foundation's name. Attest the minutes before a notary and, if desired, register the minutes in the Public Registry to strengthen enforceability. Complete any beneficial ownership declarations per SBP regulations.
required_dossiers: Registered foundation deed and Ficha
Notarial first council minutes/resolution
Passports and proof of address of council members and protector
Bank reference letters and source of endowment
Certificate of registered office address
Beneficial ownership declaration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, submit an organizational chart, source-of-wealth affidavit, and commercial references; if denied, apply to a second licensed bank. If the Public Registry queries governance minutes, notarially ratify and refile with corrected corporate formalities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Industrias; Municipalidad del Distrito de Panamá for commercial operating permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Business Operating Permit) – no separate industrial manufacturing license required for wholesale distribution of ophthalmic eyewear frames

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Verificación del Desempeño Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (No EIA required for wholesale warehousing/distribution of non-hazardous finished goods under Category I of Panama's environmental impact assessment regulations)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emission sources; operations limited to interior warehousing. Must comply with municipal solid-waste handling rules and, if applicable, Panama's general wastewater discharge regulations (Reglamento Técnico DGNTI-COPANIT 35-2000) for sanitary effluents only; packaging waste must be recycled or disposed via authorized collectors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (retrofitting of fire extinguishers, exit signage, and emergency lighting); structural load inspection of the registered office and storage area by a licensed engineer or municipal inspector; workplace occupational safety clearance per the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) regulations for safe storage, lighting, ventilation, and first-aid readiness.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama City; official portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa (RUC registration, electronic filings, Facturación Electrónica module). Export customs authority: Administración Nacional de Aduanas (ANA), operating the SIGA/VUCE single-window clearance platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) obtains its tax identity exclusively through its licensed Panamanian resident agent: (1) inscribe the foundation charter with the Registro Público de Panamá under Law 25 of 1995; (2) file the DGI RUC application (Formulario RUC) with certified charter, resident agent acceptance, legal domicile, and director/protector details; the DGI issues the 11-digit RUC which simultaneously serves as the income tax and ITBMS identifier; (3) if the foundation carries on local commercial activity, also obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación and patente comercial; (4) the resident agent files the annual B/.300 foundation tax (Ley 25, Art. 19). Foreign founders and beneficiaries never appear before the DGI; Panama has no public registry of foundation beneficiaries.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No domestic check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists in Panamanian law; the civil-law entity is fixed by Ley 25 de 1995. Panama applies a pure territorial system: Panamanian-source income is taxable at entity level at 25% corporate rate, while foreign-source income and export revenues fall outside the tax base. The PIF may elect the simplified small-taxpayer ITBMS regime where statutory thresholds are met, and may elect between refund and tax-credit treatment of excess export ITBMS. Foreign classifications (e.g., US Form 8832) are independent of Panamanian treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) – national consumption VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.0.00 (no economic turnover threshold): any person habitually or occasionally transferring taxable goods or rendering taxable services in Panama must obtain an RUC and register for ITBMS; the simplified small-taxpayer regime is an administrative collection simplification, not an exemption from registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing for substantially all registered taxpayers (phased roll-out completed January 2023). Each invoice must be transmitted through a DGI-certified software provider or the DGI portal (API/web-service integration) and receive real-time DGI online validation before delivery; the DGI affixes a fiscal stamp with digital signature and QR code. B2B invoices must be issued in standard digital format (XML/PDF-A) and retained for the full five-year prescription period; transitional paper printing is limited to marginal micro-taxpayers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods, including ophthalmic eyeglass frames, are zero-rated (0% ITBMS) when the goods physically depart Panama and are declared through the ANA customs export system (DUI export mode). Services supplied to non-residents and consumed abroad are also zero-rated when the recipient is foreign and the benefit is realized outside Panama. Outright drop-shipment from third countries directly to foreign buyers, without Panama entry, falls outside Panamanian ITBMS nexus altogether and requires no Panamanian zero-rating claim. Goods delivered into the Zona Libre de Colón are excluded from ITBMS under the free-zone regime but require separate free-zone operator authorization.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Mercancías – export DUI filed via ANA SIGA/VUCE)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical exit from Panama
Commercial invoice and packing list (HS 9003.11 / 9003.19 frame classification)
Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT MT103 or foreign bank statement evidencing settlement in US dollars)
Destination-market documentation (certificate of origin, purchase order, or distribution contract)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI may audit export zero-rating claims within the five-year statute of limitations. Unsupported or simulated exports trigger full ITBMS reversal as a domestic taxable sale, plus 1.5% monthly surcharge interest, fines up to B/.10,000 under the Código Fiscal, and ANA penalties for false customs declarations. Fraudulent refund claims are clawed back with up to 100% surcharge and referral to criminal tax fraud prosecution (2–5 years imprisonment in Panama). Missing B/L or SWIFT settlement evidence alone is sufficient basis for rejecting the zero rate.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Republic of Panama has no formal central bank. Banking conduct, AML/CFT supervision, and financial licensing are administered by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP). Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent and settlement bank for the public sector, but it does not exercise exchange-control or reserve-management authority over private cross-border flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized monetary system; the Panamanian Balboa circulates solely as a 1:1 divisional currency of the United States dollar. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible, with no central bank approval, no surrender obligation, and no foreign-exchange licensing for trade payments or profit remittances. Panama applies a territorial tax system: a Private Interest Foundation engaged in wholesale distribution of acetate eyeglass frames is subject to Panamanian income tax only on Panamanian-source commercial income. Outbound profit remittances are not exchange-control-blocked; however, if commercial income is distributed through a taxable corporate vehicle, the statutory 10% dividend withholding tax may apply. A PIF structured as a non-commercial vehicle avoids entity-level tax on foreign-source proceeds, and no remittance quarantine or prior administrative authorization exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts under Panamanian law. Export proceeds in USD or any freely convertible currency may be retained in Panamanian bank accounts, re-invoiced, or redeployed abroad without surrender to the State. For audit and tax evidence, the exporter should retain the commercial invoice, customs exit declarations (ECP/DTA), the SWIFT credit confirmation, and the underlying purchase contract to demonstrate that the receipt corresponds to a genuine wholesale optical-frames transaction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BAC International Bank, Inc. – Panama Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium, with significant structural constraints. Panama does not issue European-style e-money institution (EMI) licences; only SBP-licensed commercial banks are permitted to take deposits from the public. An offshore digital EMI cannot operate independently in Panama and cannot replace a local bank account. It may only serve as an alternative disbursement rail where the EMI is regulated in its home jurisdiction, holds a correspondent account with an SBP-licensed or internationally recognized bank, and applies equivalent KYC/AML standards. In practice, SBP-regulated banks may reject wire transfers originating from opaque offshore EMIs unless the underlying commercial purpose and beneficial ownership of the PIF are fully documented.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, at least one founding council member (or an appointed signatory with notarized and apostilled powers) must appear physically at a Panamanian bank branch or before a Panamanian notary to meet the SBP's know-your-client due-diligence standard. Remote, fully digital onboarding is not generally available for foreign-owned Private Interest Foundations. The resident agent may initiate the file, but ultimate beneficial owners must submit certified passport copies, proof of residential address, a sworn source-of-funds statement, and the Foundation Charter and By-laws showing the intended commercial purpose. The bank may waive physical presence only through a risk-based remote KYC procedure using SBP-approved biometric and video tools; such waivers are rarely granted for cross-border wholesale businesses. Therefore, the prudent blueprint assumes one in-person signatory interview and one resident-agent production of legal existence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed beneficial owner behind a nominee Foundation Council or bearer participation rights.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foundation Charter and By-laws with express irrevocable beneficiary provisions; certificate of incumbency issued by the resident agent; sworn declaration of beneficial ownership; certified passport and proof of residence for each natural-person UBO; and a corporate ownership chain chart to bank-mandated standards.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injection from a perceived high-risk jurisdiction or unregulated third-party wallet.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled Foundation resolution approving the capital contribution; source-of-funds bank statements from the remitter's regulated financial institution; commercial rationale documents; and a written declaration that the funds derive exclusively from verifiable wholesale optical-goods trade or private wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade disbursements inconsistent with the declared ISIC 4646 optical-frames wholesale scope.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed purchase orders, supply contracts, proforma invoices, commercial invoices, bill of lading/air waybill, customs export declarations, and SWIFT MT103 records linking each payment to a named acetate eyeglass frame supplier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reliance on an offshore digital EMI for treasury operations and a subsequent wire from an unlicensed payment processor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Regulatory licence of the EMI in its home state, its AML/CFT policy attestation, the PIF's own KYC pack, transactional audit trail, and a compliance memorandum from the PIF's appointed legal counsel confirming that the payment rail is acceptable under Law 23 of 2015 and SBP Accord 3-2016.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The preferred compliant routing is a direct SWIFT MT103 from the contributing shareholder's or founder's regulated bank account to the PIF's operating account at an SBP-licensed Panamanian bank. The wire's field 70 (Payment Information) should identify the transaction as 'Capital Contribution to Private Interest Foundation PA_PIF' and reference the Foundation's RUC or bank account number. Panama has no detailed national purpose-code table, but banks may require a sworn source-of-funds declaration and a council resolution. The onboarding verification file must include the Board/Foundation Council minutes, the contributor's certified identity documents, the source account statement, and an no-third-party funding undertaking. For larger injections, the bank may require a written capital contribution agreement and confirmation that the funds were cleared through an OFAC-compliant correspondent before final credit is given.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For supplier payments in optical-frames wholesale, the standard clearing rails are (i) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for open-account trade, and (ii) irrevocable documentary letters of credit issued via SWIFT MT700/MT710 for first-time or high-value supplier purchases. A commercial LC is preferred where the supplier requires title and inspection documents and where the PIF's payment history has not yet been established. USD clearing should be executed through a US correspondent bank selected by the Panamanian bank to preserve finality. For recurring platform payouts, the PIF may use a licensed bank's API-based payment gateway or an authorized processor, provided that every transaction is screened against OFAC and SBP local sanctions lists. All outbound disbursements must be backed by supplier invoices, transport documents, and purchase orders to avoid payables being recharacterized as taxable Panamanian-source activity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forwards for EUR/CNY/USD settlement with tenors up to twelve months, executed under an ISDA or local master agreement with an SBP-licensed bank.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referenced to restricted or volatile currencies, cash-settled in USD.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term matching of foreign-currency vendor financing or trade liabilities.
FX swaps (swap de divisas) for short-term liquidity conversion between USD and invoicing currencies without speculative leverage.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Tax payment under Law 25 of 1995; no separate annual return or annual report is required for a Panama Private Interest Foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 January of the following calendar year; if the Foundation has elected a non-calendar fiscal year, within the first 90 days after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge of 10% plus statutory interest; continued non-payment negatively affects the certificate of good standing and may lead to administrative strike-off by the Public Registry after formal notice to the resident agent

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None under Law 25 of 1995; an independent audit is required only if the Foundation Charter expressly mandates a supervisor or comptroller, or if financial statements are required by a beneficiary, lender, or transactional counterparty. No revenue or asset threshold automatically triggers a statutory audit for a Panama PIF.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB or US GAAP are accepted frameworks for voluntary financial statements; Panama's territorial tax model does not prescribe local GAAP for non-resident commercial activity.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual public filing of beneficiaries exists for Panama Private Interest Foundations. The resident agent must perform an annual know-your-client refresh and maintain the confidential beneficial-ownership records at the licensed registered office. Amendments to the Foundation Council or Foundation Charter must be executed by notarial protocol and, where registrable, recorded in the Public Registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members or Founders as designated in the Foundation Charter
Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required; voluntary certified audit approximately USD 2,000–4,000 depending on transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard corporate income tax rate under Panama's territorial taxation system)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial sourcing principle: income derived from extraterritorial sources is exempt; locally sourced income taxed after deductible expenses. No general statutory tax holiday for wholesale ophthalmic eyewear distribution; however, qualifying activities under Panama Pacifico or SEM regimes may access reduced rates; standard PIF entities with purely foreign-source income frequently incur zero effective Panamanian corporate income tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 104 (Declaración Anual de Renta – Persona Jurídica) filed via E-Tax (Sistema de Facturación y Declaración de la DGI), the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is within 3 months immediately following the close of the fiscal year (by March 31 for calendar-year taxpayers); a single extension of up to 2 months is available upon application; quarterly estimated payments (Declaración de Rentas Estimadas) are required for taxpayers with prior-year taxable income exceeding USD 1,000,000, due March 15, June 15, September 15, and December 15.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – General Identification (RUC, Name, Fiscal Year)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter employer tax ID (RUC), corporate legal name, fiscal period, and registered address; must match certified corporate books.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIF without Panama-sourced income: still file RUC registration update; state 'Extraterritorial Income Only' if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 – Gross Revenue from Panamanian Source
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all gross income generated from activities carried out, property located, or rights exercised within Panamanian territory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0.00 if the PIF conducts exclusively offshore wholesale trading of ophthalmic eyewear frames with no Panamanian customers, no Panamanian inventory, and no local board meetings or economic activity nexus.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 34 – Deductions (Direct Costs and Allowable Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List deductible operating expenses that are necessary to produce Panamanian-source income, including cost of goods sold, logistics, salaries, depreciation, and professional fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only deduct expenses directly allocable to any Panamanian-source revenue; extraterritorial costs are non-deductible against non-taxable income and should be excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Panamanian-source income minus allowable deductions; must reflect a true economic computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Zero or near-zero for purely offshore distribution; must reconcile with transfer pricing documentation and bank records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax due at the statutory rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute 25% only on positive Box 47; if no Panamanian-source income, enter zero.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for quarterly estimated payments, employer withholding, and other prepaid taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Self-executing; non-residents without Panamanian withholdings typically enter 0.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 58 – Final Tax Due or Credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable after credits; must be paid via electronic transfer referencing the RUC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay any positive balance by March 31 deadline; failure to pay accrues monthly interest and surcharges.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: from USD 200 up to USD 5,000 depending on gross revenue; daily surcharge of 1% per month (or fraction thereof) on unpaid tax, capped at 200% of the tax due; interest at the Banco Nacional de Panamá rate plus 3% annually; failure to file under a formal requirement can trigger criminal sanctions under the Tax Procedure Code (adaptación de la Ley No. 8 de 2010).
